parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the national layer governs entry and custody. Passport sex-marker restrictions are in force (Supreme Court allowed them Nov 2025), and the entry cable directs refusal on any document discrepancy, with a possible lifetime fraud bar. Reported passport confiscations and strandings are documented. Documented abuse in federal immigration custody includes forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse. The division's protections (gender-identity hate enhancements, marker change without medical certification, no facilities restriction, no sex-segregation law) are real but do not reach entry screening or federal custody. A documented trans prisoner placement by gender identity is an inmate-only fact. The division's sports compliance and rising risk flag are secondary. Net: elevated risk, with the division's protections mitigating only the state-sphere exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal passport marker restricted to M/F by sex at birth; new X markers stopped; discrepancy triggers refusal and document requests; possible permanent fraud ineligibility; passports confiscated or blocked, some travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; litigation pending; no documented protection operating at entry for mismatched documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal is federal and applies regardless of the division's marker-change rules, which govern only the division's own licences and birth certificates.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies from 2026 and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers. Division trans prisoner placed by gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Division placement by gender identity for its own inmate population; no documented protection for visitors in federal custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained federally cannot rely on division protections; the state-placement record does not transfer to federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal rule bars congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities. Division has no facility restriction, but the division's university system complied with national sports restrictions; a neighbouring-state trespass arrest occurred in a different unit.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division law has no restriction on sex-segregated facility use and a 2014 high-court ruling protecting school bathroom access.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funded-facility rules apply within the division, so federal buildings are exposed even where the division itself is not.

care_services.exposure: Federal subpoenas of hospital records for under-19 patients; proposed federal rule to bar reimbursement for under-18 care; federal lifeline youth services shut; sex-education funding threats.
care_services.protection: Division permits hormone therapy at 16-17 and a 2024 law protects gender-affirming care; 2026 data-collection mandate for health facilities.
care_services.interaction: Federal records and reimbursement rules reach care regardless of division protection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as priority targets; cash rewards for leadership identification; federal guidance linking 'radical gender ideology' to violent extremism; executive order directing criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Stated that counterterrorism powers will not target people who simply disagree; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-level threat framing is absent in the division, but federal framing applies to all travellers and to advocates.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minor's care and school exposure under federal prosecution threats and subpoenas; federal health rule proposals; division sanctuary bill for minors set aside in 2024 and not documented as reintroduced.
minors_guardians.protection: Division hormone access at 16-17; conversion-therapy ban for minors in the division (2019); state hate and anti-discrimination protections for minors in schools.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent or guardian accompanying a minor faces federal records and prosecution threats; division school protections cover only state-funded schools.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime enhancement for gender identity; national hate statute; 23 states cover gender identity in bias violence statutes; bias against sexual orientation is the largest share of single-bias incidents. No division-specific violence statistics.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division hate-crime enhancement, employment and public-accommodation discrimination protection, and abolition of the trans panic defence in 2019.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Strong division-level recourse; violence records for the division are not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal orders in litigation; the passport suit is unresolved; the July 2026 risk assessment's method is undisclosed; the division's risk flag increased due to sports capitulation.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Division anti-discrimination law survived two repeal referendums; division marker change without medical certification in force since 2019; public statements of support from the division's equality organisations.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Federal litigation can change entry and custody practice mid-trip; the division's protections do not cover federal entry or custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a universal, appeal-proof national visitor register with exclusion for all visibly trans visitors and no effective remedy. This dossier's entry exposure is narrower (refusal on documentary discrepancy, request for evidence) and includes some remedy through litigation, so it sits above 0.35. Federal custody abuse is comparable in severity, which keeps it below the 0.55 tier.

0.55-B describes discretionary secondary screening and administrative denial without documented custody abuse. This dossier adds documented federal immigration-custody sexual abuse and a possible lifetime fraud bar, so it sits below 0.55-B. Division protections and recourse offset some of that.

0.25-C has birth-sex housing with assaults, a criminal cross-dressing statute and documented harm in custody. This dossier has documented custody harm and a documented conversion-style federal policy, which are comparable. It lacks a criminal presentation statute in the division and gives division placement by gender identity, so it sits above 0.25-C.

parsed.synthesis: The division's strong protections (hate-crime enhancement, marker change without medical certification, no facilities restriction, 2019 abolition of trans panic defence, school bathroom ruling) are real but operate only within state-sphere systems. The national entry regime (marker-match refusal, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, reported passport confiscation) and federal immigration custody (documented sexual abuse and forced labour) apply to every visitor regardless of destination within the country. Federal facility restrictions, hospital record subpoenas and counterterrorism framing add universal exposure. Combined, the documented national exposures dominate, placing the operative regime in the elevated band, with division protections raising it above the national line but not into the reduced band.
